en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Thirteenth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether the Determined One Enters the Path of Certainty. Is it the case that one who is determined enters the path of certainty?
Yes, it is.
Does one who is fixed in falsehood enter the fixed course of rightness, or does one who is fixed in rightness enter the fixed course of falsehood?
One should not say so... [and so on].
Does one who is fixed enter the fixed course?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Does one first develop the path and afterwards enter into the fixed course of rightness?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Is it that one first develops the path of stream-entry and afterwards enters the fixed course of stream-entry?
One should not say so …pe… [and likewise for] the once-returner …pe…
[If you say that] one who is a non-returner … pe … having developed the path to arahantship, subsequently enters the certainty of arahantship—
this must not be said … pe … [end of formula].
"Does one first develop the foundation of mindfulness...
the right effort... the basis of psychic power... the faculty... the power... the factor of enlightenment, and only afterwards enter the fixed course [of salvation]?
"One should not say so... [and so on].
Is it not to be said that one who is destined enters upon the fixed course?
Yes, it is.
Is it possible that a Bodhisatta, in that birth, would not fully realize the Dhamma?
One should certainly not say so.
Therefore, he enters the fixed course of certainty.
The discussion on the certainty of the destined is finished.
